In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MUC-1951–958 is a tumor antigen against which T-cells are found frequently in BPC as well as in healthy donors.
MUC-1951–958-specific immunity is not a unique phenomenon of BCP but a frequent phenomenon in HD as well.
MUC-1951-958-specific T-cells can be found in a substantial number of BCP as well in HD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MUC-1 epitope MUC-195058 is immunogenic in a substantial proportion of patients and HD.
the immune system of BCP has the potential to generate tumor antigen-specific T-cells, but that this is often not sufficient to eradicate tumor cells.
T-cell immunity against MUC-1 is a common feature of BCP and HD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MUC-1 is a dominant tumor-associated antigen that can induce T-cell immunity in both healthy donors and cancer patients.
MUC-1 is a relevant tumor antigen against which TAA-specific T-cells are detectable in a substantial number of healthy volunteers.
